MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A customer pays with Ksh 2,000 for goods that cost Ksh 1,340. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 760
   B. Ksh 660
   C. Ksh 650
   D. Ksh 3,340

2. How can you make Ksh 50 using only 10 shilling coins? (1 mark)
   A. Five coins
   B. Two coins
   C. Fifty coins
   D. Ten coins

3. 325 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 32.50
   B. Ksh 3.25
   C. Ksh 4.25
   D. Ksh 0.32

4. How many cents are in Ksh 12? (1 mark)
   A. 1,200 cents
   B. 12,000 cents
   C. 112 cents
   D. 120 cents

5. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 3,200, Ksh 4,100 and Ksh 1,550. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 8,950
   B. Ksh 8,750
   C. Ksh 8,860
   D. Ksh 8,850

6. 450 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 4.50
   B. Ksh 45
   C. Ksh 5.50
   D. Ksh 0.45

7. Kip faces North and makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. South
   C. West
   D. North

8. Kip faces East and makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. North
   C. East
   D. West

9. A tap is usually opened by turning it (1 mark)
   A. clockwise
   B. up
   C. down
   D. anticlockwise

10. Kip faces West and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. South
   C. West
   D. North

11. At 6 o'clock the hands of a clock make (1 mark)
   A. a small angle
   B. a straight line
   C. a right angle
   D. no angle

12. How many right angles are there in a rectangle? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 3
   C. 1
   D. 2

13. How many corners does a cuboid have? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 12
   C. 4
   D. 8

14. How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 0
   C. 6
   D. 4

15. A door has four straight sides and four square corners, with two long sides and two short sides. What shape is its face? (1 mark)
   A. Triangle
   B. Circle
   C. Square
   D. Rectangle

16. What is the fold line that divides a shape into two matching halves called? (1 mark)
   A. A vertex
   B. An angle
   C. A perimeter
   D. A line of symmetry

17. In a tally chart, 3 groups of five and 1 more single tally mark are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 21
   B. 15
   C. 17
   D. 16

18. A group of five tally marks is drawn by (1 mark)
   A. five separate circles
   B. four upright strokes crossed by a fifth stroke
   C. two long lines
   D. a square

19. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. How many more are there of mango than of banana? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 7
   C. 1
   D. 3

20. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. How many are NOT swimming? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 9
   C. 11
   D. 10

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how you would find the lines of symmetry of a paper rectangle. How many are there? (4 marks)

22. A signboard has four straight sides. Two sides are 50 cm and two are 30 cm. All four corners are square. Name the shape and give a reason. (3 marks)

23. Draw a rectangle 6 cm long and 3 cm wide and label its sides. (3 marks)

24. Nanjala says an angle with longer arms is always bigger. Is she right? Explain. (3 marks)

25. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. (a) How many lines of symmetry does it have? (b) How many right angles does it have? (c) Find its perimeter. (d) Say one way in which it is different from a square. (5 marks)

26. A school uniform costs a shirt Ksh 650, shorts Ksh 800 and shoes Ksh 1,900. Find the total cost and the change from Ksh 5,000. (4 marks)

27. Amina faces south. She makes a quarter turn anticlockwise, then a half turn, then a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does she face at the end? Show each step. (5 marks)

28. Describe how you can use a folded piece of paper to test whether a corner is a right angle. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Ksh 660
   Change = amount paid − cost = 2,000 − 1,340 = Ksh 660.

2. A — Five coins
   5 × 10 = 50, so five 10 shilling coins make Ksh 50.

3. B — Ksh 3.25
   325 ÷ 100 = 3 remainder 25, so it is Ksh 3.25.

4. A — 1,200 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 12 = 12 × 100 = 1,200 cents.

5. D — Ksh 8,850
   Add the three costs: 3,200 + 4,100 + 1,550 = 8,850.

6. A — Ksh 4.50
   450 ÷ 100 = 4 remainder 50, so it is Ksh 4.50.

7. C — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a quarter turn anticlockwise gives West.

8. B — North
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. East followed by a quarter turn anticlockwise gives North.

9. D — anticlockwise
   Most taps open when turned anticlockwise and close when turned clockwise.

10. D — North
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. West followed by a quarter turn clockwise gives North.

11. B — a straight line
   At 6 o'clock the hands point in opposite directions, making a straight line.

12. A — 4
   A rectangle has four corners and each is a right angle.

13. D — 8
   A cuboid such as a matchbox has 8 corners.

14. A — 2
   It folds along the line joining the middles of the long sides and the line joining the middles of the short sides.

15. D — Rectangle
   Opposite sides are equal but not all sides are equal, so it is a rectangle.

16. D — A line of symmetry
   If the two halves match exactly, the fold is a line of symmetry.

17. D — 16
   3 × 5 + 1 = 16.

18. B — four upright strokes crossed by a fifth stroke
   The fifth stroke crosses the first four to make a group of five.

19. C — 1
   4 − 3 = 1.

20. B — 9
   10 − 1 = 9.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fold the rectangle so that the two halves match. There are two folds that work: along the middle from top to bottom and along the middle from side to side. So there are 2 lines of symmetry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for folding, 1 mark for halves matching, 1 mark for each of the two lines (or 2 marks for saying 2 with reasons).

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: A rectangle, because opposite sides are equal but not all sides are equal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the name, 1 mark for opposite sides equal, 1 mark for not all sides equal.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: A rectangle with two sides 6 cm and two sides 3 cm and square corners.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four straight sides with square corners, 1 mark for correct lengths, 1 mark for labels.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: No. The size of an angle depends on how far apart the arms are, not on how long they are.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for no, 1 mark for the opening between the arms, 1 mark for length not mattering.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 2 (b) 4 (c) 26 cm (d) Its sides are not all equal (only opposite sides are equal), and it has 2 lines of symmetry instead of 4.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for (a), 1 mark for (b), 2 marks for (c) (8 + 5 + 8 + 5 with the answer and unit), 1 mark for (d).

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Total Ksh 3,350; change Ksh 1,650
   Working / marking points: 650 + 800 + 1,900 = 3,350 (2 marks); 5,000 − 3,350 = 1,650 (2 marks).

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: North
   Working / marking points: South then a quarter turn anticlockwise gives east (2 marks). East then a half turn gives west (1 mark). West then a quarter turn clockwise gives north (1 mark). Final answer north (1 mark).

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fold a paper twice to make a neat square corner. Place its corner on the corner of the object. If it fits exactly, the corner is a right angle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for folding to make a square corner, 1 mark for placing it on the corner, 1 mark for saying it fits exactly.
